rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer: Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing ([[michael-collins]] "- [stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"). rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters of oxygen tank No. 2 ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours before launch. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board report called the switch failure a serious oversight. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The brain does not state that the board named the thermostatic switches as the cause of the fire, so I have not claimed it.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke, and his exposure set off the crew swap. The swap brought in Jack Swigert, who became Apollo 13's command module pilot in place of Ken Mattingly. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" and [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

Swigert was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but he died before taking office. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was oxygen tank No. 2. Its explosion date is in the note: [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The tank's note links it as carried by the command and service module, and that note says its service module carried the oxygen tanks: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". That fact does not name tank No. 2 itself, so the carrier link rests on the link list, not a fact line.

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted the command and service module was Michael Collins. The command and service module note links him as its pilot. His own note states: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

During the landing he stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: How many years separate Neil Armstrong's Gemini 8 command and John Young's command of the first Space Shuttle flight?
rows.answer: The gap is **15 years**. John Young commanded STS-1 in 1981, the first Space Shuttle flight [[john-young]] "[stated] Commanded STS-1 in 1981, the first Space Shuttle flight (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)". 1981 minus 1966 is 15.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Corrected: each quoted line now includes its `[stated]` tag, copied exactly from the note.

In order, the brain records these 1970 dates for Apollo 13:

1. **1970-04-10: crew swap.** A KSC management meeting decided to replace Ken Mattingly with Jack Swigert, and the swap was announced at a press conference that day. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". The Apollo 13 note records the same change: [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

2. **1970-04-11: launch.** [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

3. **1970-04-13: mission goal changed.** The lunar landing at Fra Mauro was replaced by a safe return to Earth, by a Mission Control abort decision. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The brain gives no date for the oxygen tank explosion itself.

4. **1970-04-17: splashdown.** The crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down that day. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

5. **June 1970: review board report published.** The Cortright board's report came out that month. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The brain gives no more precise date for it.
